rows.basis: Growth in gross 'Servers, network equipment, and software' (215,874m − 132,836m at June 30 2026 vs 2025). This counts all server growth, not only AI, and is gross of disposals. It excludes finance-leased assets (liability 66.6bn), leases not yet commenced (329.1bn, primarily datacenters) and purchase commitments (194.1bn), all of which are outside cash capex.

Growth in gross 'Computer equipment and software' (132,836m − 93,780m), the same category later renamed 'Servers, network equipment, and software' (both show 132,836m at June 30 2025). This counts all server and software growth, not only AI.

Growth in gross 'Computer equipment and software' (93,780m − 74,961m), the predecessor name of the server category. This counts all server growth. The FY2023 MD&A tied the capex increase to cloud and AI infrastructure only in words.
Growth in gross 'Computer equipment and software' (74,961m − 60,631m). This was largely general cloud server growth at the start of the AI buildout, so it is an upper bound on AI.
Growth in gross 'Computer equipment and software' (60,631m − 51,250m). This predates the AI buildout and no statement links it to AI; it is mostly general cloud servers and only a ceiling.

FY2026 10-K MD&A: 'We will continue to invest in capital expenditures to support growth in our cloud offerings and our investments in AI training and other infrastructure.' This is total capex with no amount or AI share.

FY2025 10-K MD&A says it will continue to invest in capex for cloud and 'AI infrastructure and training'. A Q2 FY2025 release cites 'continued investments in our cloud and AI infrastructure'. Neither gives an amount.
FY2024 10-K MD&A: capex is expected 'to increase in coming years to support growth in our cloud offerings and our investments in AI infrastructure and training'. This is total scope with no amount.
FY2023 10-K MD&A: capex is expected 'to increase in coming years to support growth in our cloud offerings and our investments in AI infrastructure'. This is total scope with no amount.

FY2026 MD&A attributes segment opex increases (e.g. +$4.9bn, +$2.5bn, +$1.4bn) and R&D (+$3.1bn) to 'research and development compute capacity, AI talent, and data' alongside Xbox impairment, sales and Copilot advertising. No AI amount is separated, and the cost-of-revenue increases attributed to AI infrastructure are not opex.

FY2025 MD&A attributes opex increases ($1.1bn, $1.5bn, $3.8bn) and R&D (+$3.0bn) to 'investments in cloud and AI engineering', in some cases together with sales and Gaming/Activision. These are total increases with mixed drivers, not AI amounts.
FY2026 MD&A: investments 'in cloud and AI infrastructure and devices will continue to increase our operating costs'. No amount.
FY2025 MD&A: investments 'in cloud and AI infrastructure and devices will continue to increase our operating costs'. No amount.
FY2024 MD&A: same sentence about cloud and AI infrastructure increasing operating costs. No amount.
FY2023 MD&A: investments 'in cloud and AI infrastructure and devices will continue to increase our operating costs'. No amount.

The Q3 FY2026 release states an AI business 'annual revenue run rate of $37 billion, up 123%'. This is a run rate at the quarter, not fiscal-year revenue, and Q4 gave none. Intelligent Cloud (137.8bn) is not AI and is not used. Commercial RPO was $678bn, a demand signal only.

The Q2 FY2025 release (quarter to Dec 31 2024) states the AI business 'surpassed an annual revenue run rate of $13 billion, up 175%'. This is a mid-year run rate, not FY2025 revenue, and likely understates the year-end level.
